newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says Japanese growth key for trade balance.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says Japanese growth key for trade balance.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Tuesday that Japan needs to focus on an economic policy mix that will produce growth in the coming months in order to affect the U.S./Japan trade balance.

"We believe the Japanese government needs to focus and is focusing on having ... a mix of macroeconomic policies that will generate growth in the months ahead and if that happens obviously this will affect the trade balance," he said.
Rubin was speaking to reporters before receiving the Citizens Budget Commission's Medal for High Civic Service in New York.
Rubin reiterated that "a strong dollar is in the interest of this country" and said it was also his view that the dollar had been strong for "quite some time."
When asked about the U.S. trade deficit with Japan, Rubin said, "The broader question is what the Japanese economy will do. There I think there is an attitude on our part of being very watchful."
Rubin said the Clinton Administration' disagreements with the Congressional Budget Office were predominantly "around what I would call economic and technical assumptions."
He also said that over the past four years, White House assumptions in these areas have been conservative.

Asked whether he shared Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's concern about excessive optimisim in financial markets, Rubin said, "Chairman Greenspan is arguing... or simply saying that people who invest should be aware of both the rewards and the risks."
